newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India fails to share local enthusiasm.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India fails to share local enthusiasm.

text.p: A five day bull run on the Bombay Stock Exchange failed to lift prices of Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) in London and premiums slid below the 20 percent mark as sellers emerged for high premium stocks.
"There is some resistance to paying 30 percent plus premiums for Indian GDRs and the underlying looks reasonably better value," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 0.77 points, 0.88 percent, at 70.50 points, with the premium over the local market at 18.45 percent compared with Friday's 21.61 percent.
The GDR market had risen about nine percent since the start of the year to Friday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 38.84 points, or 1.02 percent, to 3,453.16.

One of the few counters to gain was Reliance, up 34 cents at $13.50/$14.50, a premium of 10 percent over the local stock, while pharmaceuticals firms Ranbaxy, which announced it was to buy Croslands Research Laboratories.
Hotels group EIH Ltd was quoted at $17.75/$18.75, after a capitalisation issue in which one new share was issued for each two held.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 1.06 points, or 1.64 percent, at 65.54 points, a premium of 52.89 percent over the local market, compared with Friday's 54.08 percent.
The Korea Composite Index ended flat at 659.54.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.21 points, 0.22 percent, at 96.85, a premium of 5.71 percent after 6.11 percent on Friday.
The Taiwan Weighted Index gained 71.40 points or 1.00 percent to 7,189.47. -- David Chance, London Newsroom 44 171 542 5887
